trip.title: Tokyo & Beyond Discovery
trip.description: 7 days exploring vibrant Tokyo culture, historic temples, culinary gems, and scenic gardens.

places.name: Senso-ji Temple
places.note: Tokyo's oldest and most significant Buddhist temple, featuring the iconic Kaminarimon Thunder Gate.
places.tip: Visit Nakamise-dori shopping street early morning for photos without dense crowds.

places.name: Meiji Jingu Shrine
places.note: Serene Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji and Empress Shoken, surrounded by an evergreen forest.
places.tip: Write an ema prayer plaque near the central courtyard.

places.name: Shibuya Crossing & Hachiko
places.note: The world's most famous pedestrian scramble intersection and beloved bronze Hachiko memorial statue.
places.tip: Best elevated viewing perspective from the 2nd floor café or Shibuya Sky observatory deck.

places.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
places.note: Historic food market bustling with sushi stalls, fresh oysters, wagyu skewers, and tamagoyaki.
places.tip: Arrive around 8:30 AM before tour buses arrive. Bring yen cash for food stalls.

places.name: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
places.note: Expansive 144-acre park blending traditional Japanese landscape, English formal, and French garden styles.
places.tip: Admission is ¥500. Perfect peaceful sanctuary after lively Shinjuku streets.

places.name: teamLab Planets TOKYO
places.note: Immersive digital museum where visitors walk through water and dissolve boundaries between art and body.
places.tip: Pre-booking time slots online is mandatory. Wear clothes that can be rolled above the knees.

places.name: Tokyo Tower
places.note: Iconic 333-meter communications and observation tower inspired by the Eiffel Tower.
places.tip: Stunning illumination at night with panoramic skyline views of Mount Fuji on clear days.

days.title: Historic Asakusa & Arrival
days.dayNote: Arrival at Haneda, train check-in, and sunset stroll at Senso-ji temple grounds.
days.transportNote: Keikyu Line from Haneda Airport to Asakusa.

days.title: Harajuku & Shibuya Energy
days.dayNote: Morning at peaceful Meiji Shrine, afternoon shopping, evening Shibuya scramble.

days.title: Tsukiji Seafood & Odaiba Waterway
days.dayNote: Early breakfast at Tsukiji Outer Market, afternoon tea, Yurikamome monorail.

days.title: Shinjuku Gardens & Skylines
days.dayNote: Picnic in Shinjuku Gyoen gardens and evening skyline views.

days.title: Digital Art in Toyosu
days.dayNote: Immersive exhibition at teamLab Planets followed by waterfront dinner.

days.title: Tokyo Tower & Roppongi
days.dayNote: Afternoon ascent up Tokyo Tower and farewell celebration dinner.

days.title: Souvenir Packing & Departure
days.dayNote: Last minute shopping in Ginza, packing luggage, departure flight.
days.transportNote: Tokyo Monorail or Narita Express to airport.

transports.title: Flight to Tokyo (HND)
transports.notes: Non-stop direct transpacific flight. Baggage allowance: 2 checked bags.

transports.title: Tokyo Metro & Toei Subway 72-Hour Pass
transports.notes: Unlimited travel on all 13 Tokyo subway lines for 72 consecutive hours.

transports.title: Narita Express (N'EX) Airport Return
transports.notes: Direct airport express train with reserved seating.

packingItems.text: Passport & Japan Visit Web QR Code
Reusable tote bag for shopping & street snacks

todoItems.title: Add digital Suica / Pasmo transit card to phone wallet
todoItems.description: Enables contactless tapping on all Tokyo subways, buses, and convenience stores.

todoItems.title: Confirm teamLab Planets timed entry reservation
todoItems.description: Pre-booked for Day 5 (Oct 22 at 14:00). Save ticket barcodes.

todoItems.title: Notify bank of international travel and withdraw initial Yen cash
todoItems.description: Many traditional food stalls in Asakusa and Tsukiji remain cash-only.

todoItems.title: Download Tokyo offline maps on phone
todoItems.description: Save offline area in Google Maps for Central Tokyo, Asakusa, and Shibuya.

foodGuide.name: Tonkotsu Ramen
foodGuide.story: Rich, creamy pork bone broth simmered for 18+ hours, served with springy thin noodles, tender chashu pork, and seasoned soft-boiled egg.
foodGuide.whereToFind: Ichiran Shibuya or Fuunji Shinjuku for rich dipping tsukemen.
foodGuide.tip: Customise your noodle firmness to 'katame' (firm) for best texture.

foodGuide.name: Edomae Nigiri Sushi
foodGuide.story: Tokyo's heritage sushi style featuring seasoned vinegared rice and pristine fresh fish from Tokyo Bay and Toyosu market.
foodGuide.whereToFind: Tsukiji Outer Market stalls or Ginza standing sushi bars.
foodGuide.tip: Dip fish side down into soy sauce so the rice doesn't crumble.

foodGuide.name: Takoyaki & Yakitori
foodGuide.story: Golden octopus balls drizzled with savory sauce and bonito flakes, paired with charcoal-grilled skewered chicken.
foodGuide.whereToFind: Omoide Yokocho in Shinjuku or Asakusa market alleyways.
foodGuide.tip: Extremely hot inside when freshly cooked—eat carefully!

foodGuide.name: Matcha Wagashi & Parfait
foodGuide.story: Ceremonial Uji green tea paired with delicate handcrafted seasonal sweets made from sweet red bean paste and rice flour.
foodGuide.whereToFind: Suzukien Asakusa (famous for 7 levels of matcha gelato intensity).
foodGuide.tip: Level 7 is the richest, most intense matcha gelato in the world.

shopGuide.name: Japanese Kitchen Knife (Santoku)
shopGuide.story: Hand-forged multi-purpose culinary knife with legendary sharpness and balance, crafted by master bladesmiths.
shopGuide.whereToBuy: Kappabashi Kitchen Town (Kama-Asa or Tower Knives).
shopGuide.tip: Many shops offer free custom Japanese kanji name engraving on the blade.

shopGuide.name: Ceremonial Uji Matcha & Chasen
shopGuide.story: First-harvest ceremonial grade stone-ground green tea powder from Kyoto, paired with a bamboo whisk.
shopGuide.whereToBuy: Ippodo Tea Tokyo store in Marunouchi.
shopGuide.tip: Store in the refrigerator after opening to preserve vibrant jade green color.

shopGuide.name: Sensu Handcrafted Folding Fan
shopGuide.story: Traditional folding fan crafted from scented bamboo and painted washi paper, depicting seasonal nature motifs.
shopGuide.tip: Look for authentic 'Kyo-Sensu' mark indicating traditional production.

shopGuide.name: Japanese Stationery & Washi Tape
shopGuide.story: World-renowned smooth fountain-pen friendly notebook paper, gel pens, and decorative MT washi tapes.
shopGuide.tip: Visit the 7th floor for custom letterpress and paper tailoring.

shopGuide.name: Mino-yaki Ceramic Tea Set
shopGuide.story: Earthy, rustic glazed ceramic mugs and sake carafes originating from Gifu prefecture.
shopGuide.tip: Shop staff will pack ceramics in bubble wrap for safe flight transport.

shopGuide.name: Regional Japanese KitKats & Tokyo Banana
shopGuide.story: Unique regional souvenir sweets including Sake, Wasabi, and Hojicha KitKats, plus soft banana sponge cakes.
shopGuide.whereToBuy: Tokyo Station First Avenue or Haneda duty-free shops.
shopGuide.tip: Buy duty-free boxes at the airport after passing security.
